CHP Genel Başkanı Özgür Özel “Biz terörün sona erdirilmesine yönelik verdiğimiz katkıdan geri dönmüş değiliz ancak Adalet ve Kalkınma Partisi demokrasiye dönüş sözünden geri adım atmıştır” dedi.
Özel, 18 Kasım’da TBMM Başkanı Numan Kurtulmuş’un ziyaretinin ardından partisinin sürecin takibi için TBMM’de kurulacak izleme komisyonuna üye vermeyeceğini açıklamıştı.
DEM Parti bu kararı eleştiriyor. Nitekim dün (19 Kasım) parti sözcüsü Ayşegül Doğan şöyle dedi:
“Özgür Özel’in dile getirdiği eleştiriler sürecin demokratik zeminini zayıflatma riski taşıyor ne yazık ki. Bunun için de net bir siyasal iradeyi ortaya koymaktan geçiyor.
Sürece karşı bir kuşku ya da mesafe üretme aracına dönüştürmek barışın aciliyetine ilişkin oluşmuş toplumsal iradeyi zayıflatır. Güçlenmesini istediğimiz toplumsal iradeyi zayıflatır. İşte risklerden biri bu ve bu risk tarihsel bir risk olur. “
Barış ve demokratik çözüm sürecinde yapıcı bir rol üstleneceklerini de düşünüyoruz, buna inanmak istiyoruz. Bunun yolu süreci tartıştıracak, zayıflatacak tutumlardan uzak durmak; bundan uzaklaşmak, demokratikleşmenin ertelenemezliğini ve gerekliliğinin altını çizmek.”
Bugün Zafer Partisi Genel Başkanı Ümit Özdağ’la görüşen Özel ortak basın toplantısında YENİ Parte’nin ‘süreç komisyonu’ na katılmama nedenini şöyle açıkladı:
“İlk günden beri ‘Analar ağlamasın diye, şehitler gelmesin diye, terör bitsin diye biz bu işin içindeyiz. Kimsenin kişisel ajandasının parçası olmayız’ dedik. Komisyonda özellikle demokratikleşme adımları, fevkalade önemli. Bunlar satır satır yazıldı. 28 madde uygulandığında Türkiye’de serbest siyasetin önünde engellerin kalmayacağı, kimsenin bir cezalandırma yöntemi olarak tutuklanamayacağı, gazetecilerin içeriye atılamayacağı, mahkeme kararlarına, Anayasa Mahkemesi, AİHM kararlarına kimsenin direnemeyeceği, söz söylemenin suç olmayacağı, akademisyeninden gazetecisine, siyasetçisinden serbest vatandaşına kadar tüm özgürlüklerin sağlanacağı bir süreç varken ve bunun altına herkes imza atmışken; beylerin ağzından ne demokrasi duyuyoruz, ne adalet duyuyoruz, ne kayyımların geri verilmesini duyuyoruz.
Bu basın toplantısında TELE1, Halk TV, Sözcü TV kamerasını görmüyoruz. Muhalefetin sesinin ulaşabileceği neresi varsa onu susturmaya kalkıyorlar. Ondan sonra koca raporun altıncı kısmına endekslenip bütün meseleyi oraya sıkıştırıp ‘Gelin yeni bir komisyon kuracağız. Siz de buraya katılın’ diyorlar.
Açık açık söyleyelim: Biz terörün sona erdirilmesine yönelik verdiğimiz katkıdan geri dönmüş değiliz. Barış söylemimizden, ‘Analar ağlamasın’ söylemimizden bir adım geri atmış değiliz. Ancak Adalet ve Kalkınma Partisi demokrasiye dönüş sözünden geri adım atmıştır. Adeta milleti kandırmıştır.
Şu anda meseleyi bir yere sıkıştırıp demokratikleşme meselesine ilişkin atılması gereken adımlara ilişkin verdikleri sözü, attıkları imzayı, verdikleri oyu inkar edenlerle karşı karşıyayız. O yüzden hiç kimse dönüp de ‘Ya acaba Özgür Özel, YENİ Parti tutum mu değiştirdi’ diye düşünmesin.
Mazeret filan aramıyoruz. Bundan daha haklı bir gerekçe varsa çıksın insanlar bunu söylesinler. Kimse de bizi kendi kurdukları planın bir parçası olmaya zorlamaya kalkmasın. İktidarın gittiği yol, yol değildir. Kimse bizi Erdoğan’ın yanına davet etmesin. Erdoğan’ı demokrasiye davet edin, bütün ülke huzur bulur.
Yok Erdoğan’ın yanında konumlanmak, onunla birlikte anayasa değiştirmek, yeniden adaylığı için gerekli desteği vermek, birkaç haftayla erken seçim yapılıp ‘Erdoğan’ın önünü açalım, onu da şimdiden yapalım’ gibi planların asla parçası olmadık.
Türkiye Cumhuriyeti’nin birliği, bütünlüğü, kardeşliği, ortak ve güzel bir gelecek için herkesin eşit hissettiği, herkesin mutlu hissettiği, herkesin çocuğunun geleceğinin garanti olduğu, herkesin özgürlüğünün garanti olduğu, malının-mülkünün garanti olduğu bir düzeni inşa edeceksek, inşa edeceğiz. Etmeyeceksek, millet bunun önündeki engelleri ilk seçimde bertaraf edecek. Sonra hep birlikte bu güzel ülkeyi yaşanılabilir ve geleceğe umutla bakacağımız bir hale getireceğiz. Bu noktadaki tutumumuz nettir ve bundan sonra sorulacak soruların bize değil, Erdoğan’a yöneltilmesi gerekir.
Özel, DEM Parti’nin komisyon kararı eleştirileriyle ilgili soruya ise şöyle yanıt verdi:
“Kürt vatandaşlarımız kimin ne kadar samimi olduğunu, kimin sözünü tuttuğunu, kimin sözünden döndüğünü, kimin gerçekten kardeşçe duygularla, samimi duygularla ‘Savaş olmasın, terör olmasın, kan ve gözyaşı akmasın’ diye istediğini, kimin ise işine geldiğinde zulmettiğini, işine geldiğinde Kürt vatandaşların oy verdiği partinin eş genel başkanlarını hapse attığını, işine geldiğinde bütün seçtiği belediyelere kayyım atadığını, işine geldiğinde de ‘Gelin, bir süreç yöneteceğiz’ deyip kendisi için pazarlık yaptığını görüyor. Kürt vatandaşlarımızın buradaki haklıyı da haksızı da çok doğru ayırdıklarını biliyorum. Bu açıdan hiçbir endişemiz yok.
Esas olarak dediğim gibi yoldan sapan ya da yalan atan, verdiği sözü tutmayan, imzasını inkar eden AK Parti’dir, Recep Tayyip Erdoğan’dır, Cumhur İttifakı’dır. Sayın Bahçeli’nin zaman zaman böyle bir-iki cümleyle demokratikleşmeye yönelik küçük hatırlatmaları belki oluyor. İşte ‘Ahmetler göreve’ derken falan. Ama günün sonunda geldiğimiz nokta ortadadır. Ben milletimizin ferasetine ve öngörüsüne yürekten inanıyorum. Haklıyı, haksızı en iyi şekilde ayıracaklardır.”
PKK lideri Abdullah Öcalan, 27 Şubat 2025’te ‘Barış ve Demokratik Toplum’ adını verdiği bir metinle PKK’ya silah bırakma çağrısı yaptı. Örgüt, 11 Temmuz 2025’te silah bıraktığını duyurdu, 30 örgüt üyesi Irak’ın Süleymaniye kentinde silahlarını bir varilde yaktı .
Süreç için Meclis’te kurulan ‘Milli Dayanışma Kardeşlik ve Demokrasi Komisyonu’ nun AKP, MHP ve DEM Partili üç üyesi, 24 Kasım 2025’te İmralı Cezaevi’nde Öcalan’la görüştü . Görüşmenin tutanakları, 23 Ocak 2026’da TBMM’nin sitesinden yayınlandı .
Komisyon, 18 Şubat’ta da sürece ilişkin ortak raporu kabul etti. Bunun ardından İmralı heyeti Öcalan’la birçok kez görüştü.
Meclis, 10 Ağustos’ta PKK’nın silah bırakması için 12 maddelik ‘Milli Dayanışma ve Toplumsal Bütünleşmenin Güçlendirilmesine Dair Kanun’ u kabul etti. Kanun, 18 Ağustos’ta Resmi Gazete’de yayınlandı.
Yasa kapsamında yine süreç dört alt kuruldan oluşan Takip ve Değerlendirme Kurulu kuruldu.
O kurul, ilk kez 24 Ağustos’ta toplandı. Cumhurbaşkanı Yardımcısı Cevdet Yılmaz’ın başkanlık ettiği toplantıda şu isimler yer aldı: Adalet Bakanı Akın Gürlek, Dışişleri Bakanı Hakan Fidan, İçişleri Bakanı Mustafa Çiftçi, Milli Savunma Bakanı Yaşar Güler, MİT Başkanı İbrahim Kalın, Cumhurbaşkanlığı Genel Sekreteri Hakkı Susmaz ve MGK Genel Sekreteri Okay Memiş.
DEM Parti İmralı heyeti üyesi Pervin Buldan toplantıdan önce alt kurullar kurulacağını, Öcalan’ın da ‘silahsızlanma ve siyasallaşma kurulu’ nda görev alacağını söyledi . Fakat aynı isimde bir kurul açıklanmadı. Alt kurullardan ‘Silahsızlanma ve Stratejik Koordinasyon Alt Komisyonu’nun ismi Buldan’ın işaret ettiğine benziyor.
27 Ağustos’ta da DEM Parti İmralı Heyeti’nden Şanlıurfa Milletvekili Mithat Sancar, Öcalan’ın süreç için kurulan kurulda yer almasını beklediklerini belirtip “Önümüzdeki günlerde netleşmesini bekliyoruz” diye ekledi.
Bahçeli, 10 Ekim’de ‘siyasallaşma koordinatörlüğü görevinin Öcalan’ın hakkı olduğunu’ söyledi.

Kitap dünyasına açılan kapınızı aralayın! En sevdiğiniz kitapları indirimli fiyatlarla keşfedin ve hayal gücünüzü genişletin.
Çevre, Şehircilik ve İklim Değişikliği Bakanlığı tarafından hazırlanan Belediye Meclisi Çalışma Yönetmeliğinde Değişiklik Yapılmasına Dair Yönetmelik, Resmî Gazete'de yayımlandı.
Yönetmeliğe eklenen yeni maddeyle, belediye başkanlığı veya başkan vekilliğinin herhangi bir nedenle boşalması durumunda belediye meclisinde yapılacak seçimlerin işleyişine ilişkin yeni kurallar getirildi.
Yeni düzenlemeye göre, belediye başkanlığı veya başkan vekilliğinin boşalması halinde yapılacak seçim için vali tarafından 10 gün içinde oylama toplantısı kararlaştırılacak.
Adaylık başvuruları, ilk birleşimin ilk oturumunda meclis başkanlık divanına bildirilecek. İlk oturumun tamamlanmasının ardından yeni adaylık başvurusu kabul edilmeyecek.
Ancak adaylar, her oylama oturumu öncesinde adaylıktan çekilebilecek.
Belediye başkanı ve başkan vekili seçimleri gizli oy yöntemiyle yapılacak.
Oy pusulalarında adayların ad ve soyadları alfabetik sırayla yer alacak. Meclis üyeleri, oylarını kapalı kabinlerde tercih ettikleri adayın bulunduğu alana tercih mührü basarak kullanacak.
Seçim sürecinin yönetiminden ve düzeninden meclis başkanlık divanı sorumlu olacak.
Aday olan belediye meclisi üyeleri oylamaya katılabilecek ancak seçimin yapıldığı oturumları yönetemeyecek ve başkanlık divanında görev alamayacak.
Siyasi parti grupları ile bağımsız üyeler adına talep edilmesi halinde birer gözlemci seçim sürecinde bulunabilecek.
Yönetmelikle geçersiz oyların belirlenmesine ilişkin kurallar da düzenlendi.
Buna göre, mühürsüz veya üzerinde tanıtıcı işaret bulunan oy pusulaları ile birden fazla adaya tercih mührü basılan pusulalar geçersiz sayılacak.
Sandıktan, oy kullanan meclis üyesi sayısından fazla mühürlü zarf çıkması halinde ise ilgili turdaki seçim, zarflar açılmadan yenilenecek.
Seçimlerde kullanılan oy pusulaları ve zarflar, nihai sonuçların açıklanmasının ardından mühürlenerek muhafaza edilecek.
Söz konusu belgeler, dava açma süresinin sonuna kadar; dava açılması halinde ise mahkeme kararı kesinleşinceye kadar saklanacak.
Yeni yönetmelik, Resmî Gazete'de yayımlandığı tarih itibarıyla yürürlüğe girdi.

Gündemi BBC Türkçe'den takip etmek artık WhatsApp'ta da mümkün. Haberlerimizin doğrudan telefonunuza gelmesi için tıklayın.
Yeni Parti Genel Başkanı Özgür Özel'in, çözüm süreci kapsamında Meclis'te kurulacak İzleme Komisyonu'na üye vermeme kararı, parti içinden destek görürken siyasi kulislerde yeni tartışmaları da beraberinde getirdi.
Kararın görünür gerekçesi, iktidarın demokratikleşme taahhütlerini yerine getirmemesi. Fakat Özel'in kararı, çözüm sürecinin geleceğinin yanısıra, Yeni Parti'nin DEM Parti ile ilişkileri, milliyetçi seçmene yaklaşımı ve olası seçim ittifakları açısından da önem taşıyor.
Yeni Partililer, komisyona katılmamanın çözüm sürecinden çekilmek veya Kürt sorununun çözümüne karşı çıkmak anlamına gelmediğini vurguluyor.
Parti içinde Özel'in önümüzdeki dönemde barış ve demokratikleşme konusunda yeni inisiyatifler alabileceği konuşuluyor.
DEM Parti ise kararı sürpriz olarak değerlendirirken bunun "düzeltilebilir" olduğunu düşünüyor ve Yeni Parti ile diyaloğun sürdürülmesinden yana görüş bildiriyor.
Öcalan'ın ailesiyle fotoğrafının sosyal medyada yayımlandığı 18 Kasım Çarşamba günü, TBMM Başkanı Numan Kurtulmuş da İzleme Komisyonu'na ilişkin siyasi parti görüşmelerini Özel ile tamamladı.
Başından itibaren çözüm sürecine destek veren Özel, görüşmenin ardından sürpriz bir çıkışla komisyona üye vermeyeceklerini açıkladı.
Kurtulmuş henüz resmi yanıt almadığını belirtse de Yeni Partili siyasetçiler, karardan geri adım atılmayacağını söylüyor.
Peki Özel'in kararının arkasında hangi gerekçeler var, siyasi dengeleri nasıl etkileyebilir?
BBC Türkçe 'nin görüştüğü Yeni Partili siyasetçilere göre, Özel'in kararından önceden haberdar olan milletvekili sayısı oldukça sınırlıydı.
Ancak birçok yönetici ve milletvekili, Özel'in siyasi inisiyatif kullanmasını ve kararın zamanlamasını doğru buluyor.
Açıklamanın hemen ardından pek çok Yeni Partili, Özel'in TBMM Başkanı Numan Kurtulmuş ile görüşmesinden sonra söylediği "Biz bu işte yokuz" sözlerini sosyal medya hesaplarından paylaşarak destek verdi.
Yeni Parti, Çerçeve Yasa'nın oylamasında bölünmüştü ancak İzleme Komisyonu'na katılmama konusunda görüş birliği var.
Yasaya karşı çıkanlar süreç masasından daha önce kalkılması gerektiğini savunurken destek verenler de gelinen aşamada iktidarla aynı masada oturmanın doğru olmayacağı görüşünde.
Yeni Partililerin anlatımlarına göre kararın arkasında iki temel gerekçe öne çıkıyor: Yeni Parti'ye yönelik yargı süreçleri ve siyasi baskılar devam ederken iktidarla işbirliği yapılmasına parti tabanından gelen tepki ve iktidarın demokratikleşme konusunda samimi olmadığı düşüncesi.
Yeni Partililer, Milli Dayanışma, Kardeşlik ve Demokrasi Komisyonu raporunun 7. maddesindeki demokratikleşme taahhütlerinin yerine getirilmediğini savunuyor.
Kayyum uygulamalarının sürmesi, görevden uzaklaştırılan belediye başkanlarının görevlerine iade edilmemesi, Anayasa Mahkemesi ve Avrupa İnsan Hakları Mahkemesi kararlarının uygulanmaması, eski HDP Eşbaşkanı Selahattin Demirtaş'ın hala cezaevinde tutulması ve Yeni Parti'ye yönelik yargı süreçleri, eleştirilerin başında geliyor.
Parti içinde, belediye başkanları tutukluyken mutlak butlan kararının sonuçları ve siyasi baskılar sürerken iktidarla aynı masada bulunmanın kamuoyuna açıklanamayacağı görüşü dile getiriliyor.
BBC Türkçe 'ye konuşan bir milletvekili, Özel'in kararının yalnızca İzleme Komisyonu'na ilişkin olmadığını, iktidarın yürüttüğü sürece yönelik daha kapsamlı bir siyasi tutum anlamına geldiğini belirtiyor.
Milletvekili, "Bu sürecin artık kadük olduğu, bir sonuç doğurmadığına dair bir tavır ortaya koyuyoruz" diyor ve ekliyor:
"Gördüğümüz tek somut şey, Öcalan'ın bir yerleşkeye çıkması. Başka bir şey yok."
Yeni Parti kulislerinde, kararın arkasında seçmen tepkisinin de etkili olduğu kabul ediliyor.
Çerçeve Yasa'ya verilen desteğin özellikle ulusalcı seçmen tabanında rahatsızlık yarattığı belirtiliyor.
Deneyimli bir Yeni Parti milletvekili, parti yönetiminin yasaya destek vermesinin bağışları ve üyelik başvurularını olumsuz etkilediğini, kararsız seçmen sayısında da artış yaşandığını söylüyor.
Parti kulislerinde, ulusalcı seçmenin İYİ Parti ve Zafer Partisi'ne yönelmesini önlemenin de Özel'in kararında etkili olduğu değerlendirmesi yapılıyor.
Özel'in kararı, Yeni Parti'nin İYİ Parti , Zafer Partisi ve Anahtar Parti ile yakınlaşabileceği, buna karşılık DEM Parti ile ilişkilerinin zayıflayabileceği yorumlarını beraberinde getirdi.
Ancak parti içinde bir kesim, komisyona katılmamanın Kürt sorununun çözümüne karşı çıkmak veya siyasi çizgide sağa yönelmek anlamına gelmediğini savunuyor.
Kararın Kürt seçmene doğru anlatılması gerektiği de vurgulanıyor.
Çerçeve Yasa'ya olumlu oy veren bir milletvekili, "Biz barış sürecine karşı değiliz, Kürt sorununun çözümüne karşı değiliz. Bunu DEM'e de Kürt seçmene de anlatırız" diyor.
Yeni Partililer, Özel'in barış ve demokratikleşme konusunda yeni inisiyatifler alabileceğini, parti bünyesinde yeni kurullar oluşturulabileceğini ve somut yasal düzenlemelere destek verilebileceğini belirtiyor.
Özel'in İzleme Komisyonu'na üye vermeme kararı DEM Parti'de şaşkınlıkla karşılandı. DEM Parti kulislerinde, Yeni Parti'den bir tepki beklendiği ancak kararın bu kadar kısa sürede ve sertlikte alınmasının öngörülmediği belirtiliyor.
Yeni Parti'nin komisyon dışında kalmasının önemli bir eksiklik yaratacağı görüşündeki bazı DEM Partililer, kararın yeniden değerlendirilebileceğini düşünüyor.
Bu amaçla Yeni Parti ile yeniden temas kurulması ve kararın gözden geçirilmesi için girişimlerde bulunulması planlanıyor.
Yeni Parti'nin milliyetçi partilerle yakınlaşabileceği yorumlarına ise DEM Partililer, 2024 yerel seçimlerindeki "kent uzlaşısı" deneyimini hatırlatarak yanıt veriyor:
"Yeni Parti'yi yükselten, bugüne getiren ittifak, 2023 manevrası değil, 2024 stratejisidir. O stratejiyi biz ortaya koyduğumuzda, kent uzlaşısıyla önemli bir başarıya imza atıldı. Bunun da Özgür Özel'in hafızasında hâlâ canlı olduğuna inanıyoruz."

Çocukların eğitimden korunmaya kadar birçok hakkı var. Ancak veriler yoksulluk, çocuk işçiliği ve önlenebilir ölümlerin sürdüğünü gösteriyor. Türkiye'de de her 100 çocuktan yüzde 37'si risk altında.
Bir çocuk okula gitmenin, oyun oynamanın ve kötü muameleden korunmanın birer hak olduğunu biliyor mu?
Haklarını bilmek, başına geleni anlatmasını ve yardım istemesini kolaylaştırabilir. Onu dinlemek ve korumak ise yetişkinlerin ve kurumların sorumluluğu. Her yıl 20 Kasım'da çocuk hakları üzerine yazılar yazılıyor, açıklamalar yapılıyor. Peki bir 20 Kasım'dan ötekine çocukların hayatında ne değişiyor?
Birleşmiş Milletler (BM) Genel Kurulu, 20 Kasım 1959'da kabul ettiği Çocuk Hakları Bildirgesi'nde her çocuğun eğitim, oyun, yeterli beslenme ve barınma hakkı olduğunu ilan etti. Bildirge, çocukların ihmalden, kötü muameleden ve sömürüden korunmasını da öngörüyor.
Peki bugün Türkiye'de çocuklar yeterli beslenebiliyor mu? Okula devam edebiliyor mu? Sağlıklarına ya da eğitimlerine zarar verecek işlerden korunabiliyor mu?
BM Genel Kurulunun 20 Kasım 1959'da kabul ettiği Çocuk Haklarına Dair Sözleşme, ön sözünde 1959 Bildirgesi'ne atıf yapıyor. Bildirge'deki ilkeleri ayrıntılandıran sözleşme, taraf devletlere çocuk haklarını güvence altına almak için bağlayıcı yükümlülükler getirdi. Sözleşmenin 42'nci maddesi, devletlere sözleşmenin ilkelerini ve hükümlerini hem çocuklara hem yetişkinlere uygun ve etkili yollarla duyurma görevi de veriyor.
Sözleşmenin 12'nci maddesi, çocuğa kendisini ilgilendiren konularda görüşünü ifade etme hakkı tanıyor. Örneğin bir çocuğun kimle yaşayacağına ilişkin bir dava görülürken çocuğa görüşünü anlatma fırsatı verilmeli. Görüşüne yaşı ve olgunluğu ölçüsünde ağırlık verilmeli. Böylece çocuk, kendisiyle ilgili bir karar alınırken ne düşündüğünü ve neye ihtiyaç duyduğunu anlatabiliyor.
Sözleşmenin 27'nci maddesi, her çocuğun gelişimine elverişli bir yaşam düzeyine hakkı olduğunu belirtiyor. Devletlerin gerektiğinde ailelere özellikle beslenme, giyim ve barınma alanlarında destek sağlamasını öngörüyor.
Türkiye İstatistik Kurumunun (TÜİK) 2025 araştırmasına göre Türkiye'de her 100 çocuktan yaklaşık 37'si yoksulluk veya sosyal dışlanma riski altında. Genel nüfusta bu sayı yaklaşık her 100 kişide 28. Çocuklarda risk oranı bir önceki araştırmaya göre yüzde 38,9'dan yüzde 36,8'e gerilese de genel nüfusun yaklaşık 9 puan üzerinde. Gösterge, gelir yoksulluğunun yanı sıra maddi ve sosyal yoksunluğu ve hanedeki düşük çalışma yoğunluğunu da hesaba katıyor.
BM Çocuk Haklarına Dair Sözleşme'nin 28'inci maddesi, devlete okula düzenli devamı teşvik etme ve okuldan ayrılmaları azaltma görevi veriyor.
Milli Eğitim Bakanlığına göre 2025-2026 eğitim öğretim yılında net okullaşma oranı 6-9 yaşta yüzde 98,46, 10-13 yaşta yüzde 98,16 oldu. 14-17 yaş grubunda ise oran bir önceki eğitim yılına göre 0,67 puan artarak yüzde 87,09'a çıktı.
Okula kaydın ardından bir başka soru geliyor. Öğrenciler derslere ne kadar düzenli devam ediyor? MEB'in 2025 yıl sonu raporuna göre 20 gün veya daha fazla devamsızlık yapanların oranı genel ortaöğretimde yüzde 27,74, mesleki ve teknik ortaöğretimde yüzde 49,78 oldu. Mesleki ve teknik ortaöğretimde yaklaşık her iki öğrenciden biri en az 20 gün okula gitmedi.
TÜİK'in Hanehalkı İşgücü Araştırmasına göre 15-17 yaş grubunda ne eğitimde ne de istihdamda olan çocukların oranı 2024'te yüzde 10,8'den 2025'te yüzde 11,5'e yükseldi.
Çocuk Hakları Bildirgesi, çocukların sağlıklarına, eğitimlerine veya gelişimlerine zarar verebilecek işlerden korunmasını öngörüyor. BM Çocuk Haklarına Dair Sözleşme'nin 32'nci maddesi de devletlere asgari çalışma yaşını belirleme, çalışma saatlerini ve koşullarını düzenleme görevi veriyor.
TÜİK'e göre 2025'te 15-17 yaş grubunda 882 bin çocuk çalışıyordu. Bu yaş grubunda çalışanların oranı 2024'te yüzde 22,3 iken 2025'te yüzde 22,8'e çıktı. TÜİK'in ayrı bir çocuk iş gücü araştırmasına göre 2019'un son üç ayında 5-14 yaş grubunda çalışan 146 bin çocuğun yaklaşık üçte ikisi tarımdaydı.
İşçi Sağlığı ve İş Güvenliği (İSİG) Meclisinin kayıtlarına göre 2024-2025 eğitim yılında en az 72, 2025-2026 eğitim yılında ise en az 95 çocuk çalışırken hayatını kaybetti. 2025-2026 eğitim yılında kayda geçen ölümlerin 37'si tarımda, 27'si sanayide, 18'i inşaatta ve 13'ü hizmet sektöründeydi.
İSİG Meclisi, Eylül 2026'da sekiz, ekimde dokuz çocuğun çalışırken hayatını kaybettiğini bildirdi. İki ayda hayatını kaybeden 17 çocuğun dokuzu 14 yaşında veya daha küçüktü. Ölümlerin yedisi tarımda, dördü inşaatta gerçekleşti.
Sözleşmenin 19'uncu maddesine göre devlet, çocuğu şiddet, ihmal ve istismardan korumak için önlem almakla yükümlü. Bu önlemler,
istismarın tespit edilmesini, bildirilmesini ve soruşturulmasını, çocuğa ihtiyaç duyduğu desteğin sağlanmasını da kapsıyor.
Adalet Bakanlığı verilerine göre 2025'te çocukların cinsel istismarı suçundan başsavcılıklara 33 bin 407 yeni dosya geldi. Ceza mahkemeleri aynı yıl bu suçtan 15 bin 84 dosyayı karara bağladı. Çocuğun yardım isteyebileceği bir yere erişmesi ve süreç boyunca korunması da sözleşmenin devlete yüklediği sorumluluklar arasında.
Sözleşmenin 6'ncı maddesi, her çocuğun yaşama hakkını tanıyor. Devletlere çocukların hayatta kalmasını ve gelişmesini mümkün olan en geniş ölçüde güvence altına alma görevi veriyor.
Fikir ve Sanat Atölyesi Derneği (FİSA) Çocuk Hakları Merkezi'nin yayımladığı iki bilgi notuna göre 2026'nın ilk sekiz ayında Türkiye'de en az 542 çocuk önlenebilir nedenlerle hayatını kaybetti.
Merkezin kayıtlarına göre 133 çocuk trafik kazalarında, 57 çocuk da çalışırken yaşamını yitirdi. Aynı dönemde 31 çocuk intihar sonucu, 18 çocuk akran şiddeti nedeniyle, 12 çocuk ise bireysel silahlanmayla bağlantılı olaylarda hayatını kaybetti. Merkez, en az 60 çocuğun ölümünü de kamu kurumlarında yaşanan olaylar veya kamu görevlilerinin eylem ve ihmalleri kapsamında değerlendirdi.
27 Ocak 1995'te Resmi Gazete'de yayımlanan sözleşme, Türkiye açısından 4 Mayıs 1995'te yürürlüğe girdi. Türkiye, sözleşmedeki hakları ayrım gözetmeden güvence altına almayı ve çocukları ilgilendiren kararlarda çocuğun üstün yararını öncelikli olarak gözetmeyi üstlendi. Anayasa'nın 90'ıncı maddesi uyarınca, usulüne uygun biçimde yürürlüğe konulmuş temel hak ve özgürlüklere ilişkin uluslararası sözleşmelerle kanunlar aynı konuda farklı hükümler içerdiğinde sözleşme hükümleri esas alınıyor.
Türkiye, sözleşmenin bilgiye erişimle ilgili 17'nci maddesine, eğitimin amaçlarını düzenleyen 29'uncu maddesine ve azınlıklara mensup çocukların kültürlerini yaşama, dinlerini uygulama ve dillerini kullanma haklarını düzenleyen 30'uncu maddesine çekince koydu. Bu hükümleri Anayasa ve Lozan Antlaşması'na uygun biçimde yorumlama ve uygulama hakkını saklı tuttu. BM Çocuk Hakları Komitesi, 2023'teki Türkiye değerlendirmesinde çekincelerin geri çekilmesinin değerlendirilmesi çağrısını yineledi.

White House national cyber director Sean Cairncross will be stepping down from his role, Axios reported. The news comes as Democrats prepare to take control of Congress and as businesses across the country report a flurry of technical outages whose cause remains unknown.
Cairncross, the president’s principal adviser on national cybersecurity policy and strategy, took office in August 2025. Since then, he has met with top AI leaders and helped the Trump administration make key AI decisions, according to Axios. The outlet also reports that the split between Cairncross and the White House was amicable, and his departure was timed so that the White House could nab a Senate confirmation for his role before Democrats take control of Congress in January.
Cairncross, a lawyer and longtime Republican operative, had no cybersecurity background when the Senate confirmed him 59–35. He previously served as the Republican National Committee’s chief operating officer and, during Trump’s first term, as CEO of the Millennium Challenge Corporation, a federal foreign aid agency. The office hasn’t been around long; Congress created it in early 2021, and Cairncross was only its third Senate-confirmed director. The first director, Chris Inglis, left after about 19 months, and the job then went about 10 months without a permanent director.

Zoo staff tried a colonoscopy, vibration plate and other procedures to aid the hippo in passing the hat to no avail
Fiona the hippo, one of America’s most famous zoo animals, has died after efforts to remove a knitted hat that she swallowed after it fell into her enclosure proved unsuccessful.
“It is with extreme sadness that we share with you the devastating news that Fiona did not make it after multiple attempts from our amazing vets and keeper team to help her through what ended up being a medical emergency,” the zoo wrote in a post on social media .
With surgery too risky for full-grown hippos such as nine-year-old Fiona, who weighed in the region of 2,500lb (1,113kg), veterinarians tried an alternative method of getting the hat to pass through her system.
The hat fell near Fiona when a visitor to the Cincinnati zoo tossed it in the air, after which it bounced off a ceiling fan and fell into the enclosure, according to the Associated Press . Fiona ate the hat and was initially asymptomatic.
Days later, however, she began to lose appetite and staff at the zoo were forced to feed Fiona more in the hope that she would eventually get the hat through her digestive system.
“Despite multiple attempts to move the hat out of her system, it was ultimately too much to overcome. The team performed necessary supportive care today in an attempt to save her, but it was not successful and she did not recover,” the zoo statement said.
The zoo announced on Wednesday that the animal care team was using a vibration plate from a horse farm to help move things along, according to the Associated Press .
Fiona was sedated a second time on Tuesday for evaluation. After an ultrasound, veterinarians could see her intestines still trying to push the hat through. They also used a 9ft scope colonoscopy to view her intestines.
“The hope is that the vibrations will help encourage movement through her digestive tract and help the object pass,” the zoo had said on social media . Fiona remained out of her enclosure while she was receiving treatment.
Footage from the procedure released by the zoo on Wednesday shows her snorting and moving around her enclosure, which vets said was a sign of progress. Her hydration levels were being monitored.
Within an hour of the announcement, visitors began leaving flowers and cards by a hippo statue outside the zoo. “Forever our Fiona,” one note read.
Fiona became a global sensation after her premature birth in 2017, when she couldn’t stand on her own.
Fiona was born six weeks premature at just 29lb (13.2kgs), falling below the lowest recorded birth weight for her species at the time. Because she was initially too weak to nurse, Cincinnati Zoo staff hand-milked her mother while documenting Fiona’s recovery through photos and videos that captivated the internet.
Fiona admirers flocked to the zoo when her death was announced. Amy Haacke, a special educator from Dayton, said outside the Cincinnati Zoo that she has been a “huge fan” of Fiona since she was born because she likes underdogs. Haacke said she uses the Fiona book series in her classroom and owns three Fiona shirts.
“We were coming here anyway, but it kind of means a lot to be here,” Haacke said on Thursday. “We were here when she was first born and, I guess, now we’re here when she’s gone.”
Aftab Pureval, the Cincinnati mayor, said on social media that Fiona was “a symbol of perseverance and joy” in the city. Mike DeWine, the governor of Ohio, called her “a true icon”. The Cincinnati Bengals also expressed condolences , dubbing Fiona “the queen of the Queen City”.
The Cincinnati Reds baseball team also paid tribute : “Forever an icon. Rest in peace, Fiona.”
Chelsea Clinton, daughter of Hilary and Bill Clinton, shared her memories of Fiona and a tribute . “I will always treasure the art Fiona made for me and the smiles she gave me,” Clinton wrote.
The San Antonio zoo – whose hippo, Timothy, had a long-distance romance with Fiona – offered heartfelt condolences to the Cincinnati zoo. “Fiona held a special place in our San Antonio Zoo family and community … beyond the playful romance, Timothy and Fiona’s connection created a unique opportunity to educate audiences,” the zoo wrote. “Fiona’s impact reached far beyond Cincinnati, and the joy she brought to so many will never be forgotten.”
In a joint post with JD Vance, the US vice-president, on Instagram, second lady Usha Vance shared a photo of one of their children face-to-face with Fiona through a glass wall of her enclosure. The family has a home in Cincinnati.
“We are so sad to hear the news about Fiona,” she said in the caption. “Our family loved visiting her at the Cincinnati Zoo.”
Her survival in 2017 had offered a much-needed positive chapter for the zoo following months of intense public backlash over the fatal shooting of Harambe , the silverback gorilla killed after a child breached his enclosure.
Wildlife facilities have long warned of the dangers posed by foreign objects dropped or blown into animal habitats. Past incidents have demonstrated the fatal risks involved, including a rare antelope that choked to death on a plastic cap of a snack pouch at a Tennessee zoo two years ago, and a polar bear at a German zoo that died in 2014 after swallowing a visitor’s dropped jacket.

Kirsten Davies, the defence department's chief information officer, is set to take over from Cairncross on a temporary basis, the source said.
"Congratulations to the new National Cyber Director Kirsten Davies — look forward to working together to strengthen America’s cybersecurity," US Secretary of State Marco Rubio wrote in a post on social media.
At the Pentagon, Davies has acted as the "principal advisor" to Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth "on all matters relating to information management, information technology, cybersecurity, and information assurance," her bio says.
The move comes after outages have hit travel, communications and banking, as well as an internal system used by the National Security Agency in recent weeks.
The national cyber director is tasked with advising the president on cybersecurity policy and strategy, including information security and data protection as well as deterrence of "malicious" activity.
The director also coordinates cyber policy across the federal government. The office was first established in 2021.
In March, the Trump administration released a seven-page document detailing its cyber strategy.
It pledged to "act swiftly, deliberately, and proactively to disable cyber threats" by streamlining cyber regulations, modernising federal information systems, hardening critical infrastructure and maintaining an edge in AI.

From premature baby to social media star - Famed Cincinnati Zoo hippo Fiona dies
The Cincinnati Zoo in Ohio says its beloved hippopotamus Fiona has died just days after swallowing a knitted hat that slipped into her enclosure.
"It is with extreme sadness that we share with you the devastating news that Fiona did not make it after multiple attempts from our amazing vets and keeper team to help her through what ended up being a medical emergency," the zoo said on Thursday afternoon.
Fiona, who became a social media star after her premature birth in 2017, swallowed the hat about 10 days ago and required emergency care.
The vet staff "tried everything they could to help her" but "it was ultimately too much to overcome", the zoo said.
Fiona initially seemed fine after swallowing the hat more than a week ago
"We are in shock at the moment," Cincinnati Zoo director Dave Jenike said in a statement. "We did not expect this outcome. She fought until she couldn't anymore."
Michelle Curley, a spokesperson for the zoo, had said that the hat got into Fiona's enclosure by accident, after a visitor tossed it in the air and it caught on a ceiling fan that flung it through a small opening.
"We probably couldn't make [it] happen again if we tried," Curley said.
While she seemed fine at first, her appetite started to decrease a few days later, and the zoo staff tried to encourage Fiona to eat to help push the hat through her digestive system.
An ultrasound before her death showed the hat passing through Fiona's small intestine. A zookeeper said surgery was not an option for full-grown hippos and "our best chance for success with Fiona would be if she could pass this on her own".
The zoo also tried a different approach to attempt to get the hat to pass by encouraging Fiona to stand on a vibration plate platform borrowed from a local horse farm.
"Our animal care team was heroic in their efforts to save her. They did everything possible, but her body couldn't fight anymore," Jenike said.
Fiona was born premature at the Cincinnati Zoo in 2017 and at first struggled to survive. At birth, she weighed 13 kg (29 lbs), which the zoo said was about half the previous lowest recorded birth weight for her species.
Her death is also very premature, with hippos normally living up to 50 years in human care, according to the zoo.
"Although this was not an intentional incident, of which, regrettably, there are many, Fiona's painful death is a tragic reminder that everyone should behave carefully and respectfully around animals," said Debbie Metzler, the managing director of captive wildlife for the animal rights group People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (Peta).
"Peta expects that the zoo will review its protocols to help prevent anything like this from happening again, and we urge every visitor to secure their belongings and never toss objects near an animal's enclosure."
As well as being famous online, Fiona's story inspired an ice cream flavour and a character in Cincinnati's ballet.
Cincinnati Mayor Aftab Pureval said Fiona "was a symbol of perseverance and joy" in the city.
"She brought smiles to so many faces, from kids to parents to visitors from around the world," he wrote on X. "Our city is heartbroken, but we couldn't be more grateful that she was part of our lives and our community as a whole."

Anthropic has become one of the most valuable public companies in the world after its shares began trading on the stock market, taking its valuation to roughly $1.76 trillion (£1.34 trillion).
The artificial intelligence (AI) company's Thursday debut on the Nasdaq stock exchange was a crucial test for the industry, given the huge amount of money being poured into advancing the technology.
Anthropic's shares flew past its allocation price of $83 each , showing there was plenty of excitement around AI.
Yet the company, which is behind AI chatbot Claude, will remain under intense scrutiny in the months ahead to answer the key question surrounding AI: is it all worth it?
In just a few hours of trading, Anthropic's stock seemed to show that investors remain uncertain of where exactly AI is heading. The share price rose immediately to $111.53, sending the company's market value to almost $2 trillion, before falling by the end of the day as the shares closed at $97.17.
Some investors said Anthropic's debut seemed to be a success, as shares rose roughly 17% during the day, but the broader tech market did not perform as well.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index closed down nearly 2.3%. Stocks fell in the largest tech firms, including Google's parent company Alphabet, which was down by 2.9%, while Amazon lost almost 3.9%.
The buildout happening around this era of AI is among the most expensive endeavours in the history of technology, with more than $1 trillion being spent in the last year alone by a handful of major tech companies.
The speed at which investment has grown has led to ongoing concerns of a financial bubble.
"Bubbles don't burst on the day of the largest deal," Richard Whittle, an economist with the University of Salford said. "They burst later, if the positive future becomes suspect."
Anthropic has made one of the fastest trips from start up to IPO in history
While the basics of the technology have been around for decades, the more recent advent of more powerful computers and related components have allowed the processing of more data than ever.
The result has been AI chatbots that simulate human speech and operate tasks like software coding, digital image generation, and searching the internet more quickly.
It represents a new way of using computers that has led to the rapid rise of Anthropic, which started just five years ago and is best known as the maker of the popular AI chatbot Claude.
As the first purely AI company to go public, Anthropic will almost certainly see significant swings in price on the stock market going forward, according to Ben Barringer, who leads technology research at Quilter Cheviot.
The "initial exuberance" will wear off, Barringer said, pointing to what happened with SpaceX earlier this year.
That company, led by Elon Musk, saw shares jump by about 10% on the first day of trading, taking the company to a record-breaking valuation of $2.2 trillion.
Within a month shares had fallen below their debut price, and have mostly fallen further since.
Most tech companies see their shares fall after hitting the stock market, often after reporting quarterly results for the first time.
But many such companies, including Meta, Amazon and Google, have gone on to become the largest and most profitable corporations in the world.
With Anthropic, investors are not only looking at a notable tech company with a major valuation, and a potentially big future in business, but a company that is the first of its kind on the stock market.
"There's no obvious peer to compare it to," Neil Wilson, an investor strategist at Saxo UK, said.
Simon Jack: Can Anthropic's record-breaking IPO stop the AI bubble bursting?
So, as individual investors and even researchers and investors at large funds ask themselves if Anthropic is really worth more than $1.7 trillion, or even more, there will be few answers available.
"We'll have a stab at it," Wilson said. "I don't think anyone really knows."
A few things will likely impact the company's success on the stock market in the near-term.
One of those things is the prospect of new laws governing the use of AI tools. In the US, where Anthropic is based, Democrats will be in many more positions of power come 2027, and several politicians have already said they will be looking to ensure AI tools are safe and have some guardrails attached.
Such regulation is currently unlikely at the federal level. US President Donald Trump on Thursday spoke about AI during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in China, alongside Chinese and Russian counterparts, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin.
Trump reiterated his position against "any form of robust regulation" around the technology, adding, "we won't allow that to happen, frankly."
The same day, however, a bipartisan group of US lawmakers formed the House AI Safety and Innovation Caucus, which will work specifically on AI regulation and safety considerations.
A significant driver of this kind of scrutiny is Anthropic itself. Company executives, including co-founder and CEO Dario Amodei, have been outspoken in their purported fears that future AI tools will become so capable they will outsmart humans, to the point where extinction is possible.
Anthropic has always put itself forward in public as an AI company that takes the safety of its technology very seriously.
Daniela Amodei, Anthropic's president and sister of Dario Amodei, boasted on Thursday that the company "had an AI safety team before we launched our first product".
Despite the company's claims that the technology it is building at a rapid pace could be dangerous, Anthropic has made one of the quickest trips from start-up to IPO in history.
Anthropic raises $81bn in record-breaking stock market debut

A record breaking IPO has raised billions for the AI frontier lab – but experts say the coming months could prove bumpy, as the industry faces a variety of challenges
Anthropic closes first day of public trading at $1.3tn valuation after largest-ever IPO
In the end, Anthropic’s much-anticipated IPO more than lived up to the hype. The market’s embrace of one of the AI industry’s most talked about companies has resulted in the maker of the Claude chatbot becoming one of the world’s most valuable firms after just one day of trading.
With many of the company’s founders, investors and employees now worth billions of dollars – and demand for the company’s stock remaining resilient – attention now turns to the stability of the wider market, and the global headwinds that experts say could threaten the AI industry over the coming months.
Here’s a rundown of what we can gather after a big day for Anthropic and the AI industry
Closing the day about 17% higher than its initial public offering price, Anthropic shares were trading at just over $97 when the market closed taking its valuation to roughly $1.7tn. The share price initially soared by 34% when trading got under way on Thursday, briefly taking the company’s valuation to more than $2tn.
The blockbuster debut easily places the IPO as the biggest in history , with the 980m shares sold raising $81bn, surpassing the previous record held by Elon Musk’s SpaceX’s $75bn raised in June.
Despite the excitement, major US stock indexes fells to seven-month lows on Thursday, dragged down by growing concerns about the longer-term outlook for the AI industry.
“The blockbuster Anthropic launch is a critical step in reassuring the market about the potential for AI, but ​it’s really just the beginning,” said Bob O’Donnell, chief analyst at TECHnalysis Research.
double quotation mark We still need to see ‌what happens with OpenAI, how the Nvidia situation evolves , how ‌the political climate for data centres shapes up, and what the historical performance for Anthropic proves to be before we’ll get any real sense of stability.”
In early trading on Friday, Asian stocks plunged by up to 4%, suggesting Anthropic’s debut has done little to settle nerves on trading floors.
According to reports demand for Anthropic shares was about six times what the company was able to offer, an incredible result for a company founded in 2021.
Started by a number of former OpenAI employees, Anthropic initially lagged behind its rival frontier lab, but analysts say its focus on building software for business and programming clients has helped to position it as one of the market leaders.
That breakneck growth has left investors stunned; from fledgling start-up six years ago, Anthropic is now worth more than US stock market stalwarts Walmart, JP Morgan, Visa and ExxonMobil.
The speed of its growth is reflected in its revenue: according to its investor prospectus, Anthropic brought in $16.2bn in the first six months of 2026, up from $4.6bn in revenue for all of 2025.
But Anthropic has also lost an enormous amount of money. In the first half of 2026, the company reported losses of $80bn, though that was largely due to a one-off charge. Losses grew to $104bn in the first nine months of 2026. The firm has said its costs will balloon as it invests further in datacentres.
The IPO hands Anthropic a pool of new cash to make those investments, but with promises to spend about $900bn on datacentre infrastructure over the next two decades, experts say their debt is likely to rise even further.
Newly minted Anthropic investors will also have to contend with rising public sentiment against AI.
Anthropic’s CEO Dario Amodei has been among the loudest voices pointing out the dangers that the products he and his rivals are developing may pose to humanity. He has called for a slowdown on the development of the most advanced AI models after employees expressed concerns that they were being built irresponsibly.
Across the US, opposition to AI companies has manifested in protests against local datacentre plans , with a number of municipalities and states voting for bans or restrictions on them at the recent midterm elections.
US economic growth is inextricably tied to the booming AI sector, and in particular the vast investments in datacentres that power programmes like Claude and ChatGPT. One estimate from Harvard professor Jason Furman suggested “investment in information processing equipment and software” accounted for 92% of the US’s GDP growth in the first half of 2025.
Any slowdown in that expenditure on datacentres could therefore have far-reaching consequences for Anthropic – and the global economy.
Anthropic’s leaders are also likely looking ahead to the changes to government next year, when Democrats take over both chambers of Congress after securing large majorities in the midterm elections.
Senior Democrats have already suggested that tech companies could face a regulatory crackdown over the dangers that advanced AI models pose, and over the volatility that AI IPOs could introduce into the economy.
Last month Democrat Elizabeth Warren, a senior member of the Senate banking committee, appeared to signal such moves, telling Amodei in a letter that Anthropic’s IPO “could inject extreme volatility and risk into the financial system, which threatens to undermine Americans’ economic security.”
double quotation mark The fact that Anthropic is burning through cash and requires an insatiable stream of capital to feed its growth is not a reason to expose everyday Americans to the company’s risks in our public stock markets … Swings in Anthropic’s share price have the potential to roil the broader markets on day one.”
Jensen Huang – the former CEO of Nvidia, the most important company in providing the advanced chips that power AI – is due to appear before Congress next month. He’ll be answering questions about his affair with a suspected Chinese spy, a scandal that has resulted in the loss of one of Silicon Valley’s key figures and sparked bipartisan national security concerns.
Earlier this year Anthropic’s chief rival, OpenAI, decided to postpone its initial offering until 2027. Experts say that Anthropic’s market reception and the movements in its share price will act as a signal to others in the industry over what the appetite for another large AI IPO will be.
Earlier this week, Open AI CEO Sam Altman said his company will go ahead with the IPO next year, even in the face of increased volatility.
Speaking to US publication Semafor, Altman appeared to take comfort from the sheer demand for Anthropic shares, leading up to Thursday’s stock market debut. “There’s been way too much investor demand and not enough supply,” he said.

Fiona, the Cincinnati Zoo’s famous hippo who charmed observers around the world, tragically died on Thursday due to medical complications after ingesting a knit hat that mistakenly entered her enclosure last week, according to zoo officials. Fiona was just nine years old when she died.
According to zoo officials, the hat that caused her death entered her enclosure after a child tossed it into the air. The hat reportedly collided with a ceiling fan, which then launched the hat through a “one-foot gap above the 12-foot-tall viewing window." A few days after eating the hat, her condition began to deteriorate.
For nonexperts, Fiona’s tragic death raises several questions: Why and how would a knit hat kill a hippo that weighs more than 2,500 pounds? Why wasn’t surgery possible for Fiona? And for zookeepers, what was the range of treatment scenarios available?
Jan Hawkins, the head of the the clinical science department at North Carolina State University's College of Veterinary Medicine, tells WIRED that—with the caveat that we won’t officially know until doctors conduct a post-mortem analysis—Fiona’s death was likely due to one of a few downstream effects of the hat getting caught somewhere in her intestinal tract.
In a sense, an intestinal blockage in a hippo is like a car crash on an incredibly long one-lane highway. Hawkins said that, estimating, a hippo’s intestinal tract is likely over 100 feet long, with more than 70 feet in the small intestines alone. In humans, the lengths of the small and large intestines are a comparably diminutive 25 feet.
Hawkins says that in a healthy hippo, liquids can take as little as 12 hours to pass, and food takes two to three days. According to zoo officials, Fiona ate the hat on or about Sunday, November 8. Zoo officials claimed that Fiona was asymptomatic at first, but began to lose her appetite after a few days. If the hat was going to come out, Hawkins says it likely would have happened within five days. So what happened?
One possibility, Hawkins says, is that when the hat got stuck, it caused a huge amount of swelling and pressure in her abdomen. That swelling could have led to her blood circulation being cut off, and eventually, to tissue death. After becoming green or black, Hawkins says that dead tissue is more likely to leak, and perhaps rupture, releasing the contents of the digestive tract into her blood. This can easily cause toxic shock.
In Fiona’s situation, this would mean that bacteria in her digestive tract died and released toxic molecules. Hawkins says that if these toxins enter the bloodstream, it would cause the organs to become more and more inflamed. Ultimately, this can lead to organ failure and death.
Another possibility is that, after the hat got stuck, Fiona’s intestines began to “twist on itself,” Hawkins says. This would be more likely if the hat, say, got pieces of food stuck inside of it, gradually becoming larger and heavier. Intestines are supposed to contract and move as they digest food. This means that if a heavy object gets stuck, the intestine can start to twist around it. In severe cases, this can cut off blood circulation. Eventually, this too can lead to tissue death. This initiates the chain of intestines leaking or rupturing, toxins entering the bloodstream, and organs becoming inflamed and eventually failing.
We don’t know exactly where the hat was in Fiona’s digestive tract. However, in a video the Cincinnati Zoo published to X on Tuesday, an unnamed staffer claimed that an ultrasound showed “some bunching of intestines.” They believed this meant that Fiona was “passing some things through her small intestine.”
If the hat was in Fiona’s small intestine, this would have meant that it passed through all three of her stomachs. (Hippos have three stomachs.) This could provide some hints about the type of hat that Fiona ate.
Hawkins says that in hippos, all three of their stomachs have the same basic components, but in different amounts. The first stomach has the largest amount of bacteria and protozoa, which help break down big pieces of food in the earliest part of digestion. The third has the highest amounts of enzymes and hydrochloric acid, which reduce food scraps into their smallest-possible size before entering the small intestine.
“Let's say it was a cotton hat or some sort of organic material, it's possible that that could partially break down,” Hawkins tells WIRED. “Whereas if it had something that would not degrade—so a plastic, or polyester, or something like that—then obviously its character is not gonna break down at all.”
The effects of this, Hawkins says, would be even more severe if the hat was rigid, or not collapsible in any way. “If it wouldn't get scrunched down, like a hair scrunchie, then you could understand why it would get stuck,” Hawkins says. “Because it can't change its character as much.”
All of this, Hawkins says, may have affected whether Fiona was able to pass the hat.
According to the Cincinnati Zoo’s Tuesday video , conducting surgery to remove the hat would not be possible for Fiona. The zoo claimed that a combination of specialists—including “veterinarian human specialists,” zoo employees, and “other experts”—came to the conclusion that surgery wasn’t the best option, and that the “best chance for success with Fiona would be if she can pass this on her own.”
Rebecca Lewison—San Diego State University biology professor, and co-chair of the Hippo Specialist Group of the International Union for Conservation of Nature—tells WIRED that when it comes to hippo surgery, a major challenge is their “unpredictable and irregular responses to sedation and anesthesia.”
“It is very risky for [hippos], and they can die from the standard medication used on other large animals, like elephants and rhinos, for reasons we don't well understand,” Lewison tells WIRED.
There are also some inherent challenges to administering anaesthesia on an animal as large as Fiona. When a human or animal goes under anesthesia, they need to be put on a ventilator that artificially breathes for them. An animal that weighs more than 2,500 pounds, Hawkins says, requires a ventilator of a much different scale than what humans need for general surgery.
Fiona was placed under anaesthesia to conduct bloodwork, according to the Cincinnati Zoo’s Tuesday video . But Hawkins says that the amount of anesthesia required for bloodwork is much smaller than what would be required for a major surgery, like removing a foreign object from her intestines. For Fiona, the increased amount of anaesthesia alone increases the risk of the surgery.
Another fact to consider, Hawkins says, is the position the zoo would feasibly be able to place her in while conducting surgery. If a human is in surgery, they may be placed on their back, their stomach, on their side, or in a variety of other positions. With animals like hippos, Hawkins says, this gets more complicated.
“You would have to have a hoist, a forklift or something, to pick them up to put them on either a pad or on a table,” Hawkins says. And if a zoo doesn’t have a table that’s big enough, the animal may have to go on the floor.
But Hawkins says that even at perfectly resourced zoos, there are other risks for hippos. In order to perform a major surgery, an animal as large as Fiona would have to have a huge amount of anaesthesia, putting her unconscious, and in the same position, for a long period of time. She would have her entire body weight putting pressure on the parts of her body that can’t move. This would limit her body’s ability to circulate oxygen—even with the help of a great ventilator.
If an animal is unhealthy, Hawkins says, the risks are even greater. In its Tuesday video , the Cincinnati Zoo said that when it recently ran some tests on Fiona, it found that she was dehydrated. This means that her body was already working extra hard to circulate blood not only to the blockage, but through the rest of her body.

Apple appears to be working on its own AI agent to conduct computer work on behalf of users — including using apps, accessing websites, and coding, among other things.
The news was originally reported by Bloomberg, which spotted a job listing the iPhone maker recently posted for a senior engineering manager to oversee the creation of an “AI agent that can use a computer.”
“Imagine an AI agent that can use a computer the way a capable person does,” the posting says. “It browses the web, works across apps, runs commands, writes and debugs code, and calls services, and it chooses the right tool for each step. It does all this privately and with the polish people expect from Apple.”
The posting additionally notes that the agents should be able to move “fluidly between tools” and “carry out multi-step tasks across apps, browsers, command lines, code, and APIs.”
TechCrunch reached out to Apple for more information but did not receive a response.
Agents capable of computer work have become one of the hottest commodities in the tech industry over the past year. Major labs like Anthropic and OpenAI have launched such services, while other major tech brands — like Meta, which recently launched its Muse agent line — have also moved into the space. It makes sense that Apple — which is trying to expand its AI offerings in the new John Ternus era — would want to follow suit.
Bloomberg additionally notes that, at the same time that Apple is working on its own digital assistant, the company is making it significantly harder for third-party agents to gain total control over its computers.
The outlet notes that the version of its upcoming macOS 27.3 will deploy warnings discouraging users from granting full access to third-party agents. In October, Apple issued a notification to developers stating that the company planned to “introduce additional controls to ensure that users who genuinely wish to grant an app this extraordinary level of access can only do so with very explicit user action.”
Bloomberg writes that while the iPhone maker “has eyed introducing the service as soon as the end of next year,” progress on its in-house agent “remains in the early stages.”

Apple’s job listing describes an AI agent that can browse the web, work across apps, and call services.
Apple is working on its own AI agent that can perform a range of tasks for you, including browsing the web, working across apps, writing code, and calling services. That’s according to a job listing spotted by Bloomberg , which says Apple is looking for an engineer to lead the creation of an agentic AI assistant.
An AI agent from Apple would put the iPhone maker in the running to compete with the likes of Meta’s Muse , OpenAI’s Dots , Anthropic’s Duet , and Google’s Tasks . Muse, ChatGPT, and Perplexity can already take control of a computer through their Mac apps, while Google just started letting Gemini do the same.
Apple began rolling out its AI-upgraded Siri in September, which you can use to ask questions about what’s on your screen, as well as perform actions across apps. It looks like Apple is planning to give Siri more agentic capabilities , as a report from Bloomberg suggests the company could add the ability to rotate and crop images in Photos, or organize Safari tabs. This lines up with the company’s new job listing, which says the engineer will work closely with teams across its Siri, UI Frameworks, and Apple Foundation Models divisions.
“People already do their most valuable work by moving fluidly between tools: a browser, a document, a terminal, an editor, a service,” the job listing says. “We’re building AI agents that can do the same… These agents plan and carry out multi-step tasks across apps, browsers, command lines, code, and APIs, and they can coordinate specialized sub-agents along the way.”
With its upcoming iOS 27.3 update , Apple is also giving developers the ability to integrate Siri AI into “all apps.” This is rolling out as part of a Developer Preview and will eventually allow Siri to perform tasks across a wider range of apps.
texts.https://www.wired.com/story/muse-is-unle:
Khalil Roberts had heard horror stories of people getting kicked off Instagram for using third-party apps to purge follower counts, so when he came across an X post claiming that Muse — Meta ’s AI assistant —could mass-unfollow people who didn’t follow him back, he didn’t believe it.
“I’ve never gone through my exact list to vet those people out, but I’ve always been curious,” the 31-year-old New Yorker tells WIRED. But after realizing that by using Muse, his account wouldn’t get flagged as spam, his mind was made up. “I was like, I actually will be a little petty.”
After downloading Muse, Roberts, who had over 7,600 followers, entered the prompt: “Can you show me a list of people (non celebrity) that [don’t] follow me back on instagram and can you unfollow them for me. ”
Within minutes, Muse identified 151 accounts. It attached an Excel sheet with a breakdown of everyone cataloged—separated by categories identifying their username, real name, classification, and profile link—and asked if Roberts wanted to proceed with his request. Shockingly, some of the names were people he thought of as friends. “It was a little surprising, but also a reminder that we don’t have a relationship anymore.”
Following the success of his November 7 cleanse, Roberts posted about it on X, offering instructions to his followers. Over the past several weeks, parallel scenarios have played out across X, Instagram, and Facebook, with users sharing tips on how to automate their unfollows with the help of Muse.
X user @justdrmj posted about the trend the same week as Roberts, and nearly every reply shared a taste for trivial grudge-holding. For him it came down to one simple rule: “Why be a fan?” “i agree. reciprocity is key,” one person said in response. “The way I just cleaned house,” added another . In a seeming outburst of celebration, one X user posted : “Just unfollowed 1000+ people on IG.”
Even tech worker Kimberly Munoz, who has 33,200 Instagram followers, said she wasn’t about to be “anybody’s fan,” noting in an Instagram video that she used the feature to suss out “people that I know in real life that have unfollowed me.” “I downloaded Muse just to do this only,” one person responded.
With social media rapidly evolving, there is no longer a unified consensus around etiquette. For some people, following others is an indication of friendship or simply a way to keep tabs on your latest crush. Others view it as more of a social obligation—you follow someone if they follow you, but the opposite is true as well.
Natalie Pennington, an associate professor who researches social connection at Colorado State University, wonders about the consequences of people gradually outsourcing small social decisions to technology.
“It is probably at least partially a question of not wanting to deal with emotionally uncomfortable things,” Pennington says. “This also strikes me as another example of information we don’t really need that social media can give us. There’s this data that exists at the platform level or would take a lot of effort to find out on your own, but now you can learn with the click of the button. But it doesn’t mean it is something you need to know.”
In October, despite the seeming popularity of the feature, Meta removed an advertising campaign that promoted Muse with the promise that users could “ see who unfollowed you each week ,” Business Insider reported .
When WIRED asked about the reasoning behind Meta’s decision to remove the ad, the company did not respond to a request for comment.
But Muse’s capabilities aren’t just being employed to even scores. Some people are using the assistant to streamline feeds that have become extremely cluttered over the years.
Elizabeth Brooks is a self-proclaimed “sweeper”—the term for a hobbyist who routinely enters sweepstakes and promotional contests—who, over the course of 10 years, had followed various accounts offering giveaways. Recently, she started prompting the assistant to bring her five profile links every few hours, no more than six times a day, for her to manually unfollow one by one. “Your following list can finally work for you instead of the other way around,” she wrote on Facebook .
Roberts, who joined Instagram in high school 15 years ago and calls the platform “my app of choice,” says people are becoming more intentional about their digital relationships and who they let into their online lives. But he doesn’t plan on letting Muse make any more decisions about his social life, he says.

Asian markets on track for their worst week since 2020, with European and US stocks also way down
Global stock markets have slumped as Anthropic’s record-breaking IPO failed to stem a sell-off in AI-linked companies.
Asian stock markets were on track for their worst week since 2020, as shares in big chip companies fell on Friday. In Taiwan, stocks dropped 6.7% to hit their lowest point since mid-April, with the chip maker TSMC down about 6%.
The scale of the decline in Taiwan prompted the chair of its stock exchange to pledge to ensure the stable operation ⁠of capital markets, and reassure investors they should remain confident in the fundamentals of Taiwanese companies.
In Japan, the Nikkei index fell 5%, while South Korea’s tech-heavy Kospi index lost 5.5%. Shares in the tech investor SoftBank had their worst day in more than two years, down 14.5% in Tokyo, amid worries around its aggressive bets on AI.
European stock markets were heading for their worst week since March, with the pan-European Stoxx 600 dropping 1.3% in the first 90 minutes.
The sell-off followed losses on Wall Street on Thursday, where the main indices all fell by more than 2% on a day dominated by Anthropic’s IPO .
Anthropic’s shares jumped by 17% on Thursday, after briefly surging by almost 40% when trading in the frontier AI firm began. But they were heading for losses on Friday, down 6% at $91.30, falling back towards the IPO price of $83.
Chris Beauchamp, the chief market analyst at the investing and trading platform IG, said Anthropic could be “draining market liquidity”, as investors sell shares in other companies to raise funds to pay for stock in the newly floated AI firm.
“The slide from yesterday’s highs sends a message that there might be more at work here than investors realise, and while brokers are scrambling to buy more, that liquidity has to come from somewhere, and the other tech names may be the first ones to feel the pressure,” Beauchamp said.
Anthropic’s flotation has failed to ease worries around the AI trade, as investors increasingly question whether companies can deliver the returns necessary to justify the billions of dollars being poured into the AI build out.
Daniela Hathorn, a senior market analyst at Capital.com, said: “The IPO demonstrated that demand for AI exposure remains strong, but it has not been enough to overcome concerns about elevated valuations, profitability and the sustainability of investment spending.
“The broader market mood has shifted from buying the dip towards questioning whether the correction has further to run. The weakness in equal-weighted indices suggests that selling pressure is no longer confined to a handful of technology giants, while Europe’s recent outperformance has also faded.”
Britain’s FTSE 100 share index hit a five-month low on Friday morning. It has dropped by 4.8% this week, and is heading for its biggest weekly fall since the start of the Iran war.
Fears that US central bankers may raise interest rates to fight inflation have lifted the dollar to a 19-month high, and pushed down the gold price – with gold on track for its worst week since March.

Kitap dünyasına açılan kapınızı aralayın! En sevdiğiniz kitapları indirimli fiyatlarla keşfedin ve hayal gücünüzü genişletin.
Apple, yapay zekâ alanındaki rekabetini yeni bir aşamaya taşımaya hazırlanıyor. Şirketin, kullanıcıların verdiği görevleri kendi başına yerine getirebilecek “genel amaçlı bilgisayar kullanım ajanları” üzerinde çalıştığı ortaya çıktı.
Apple’ın internet sitesinde yayımladığı yeni iş ilanları, şirketin otonom yapay zekâ sistemlerine yönelik hazırlıklarını gözler önüne serdi.
Apple’ın yayımladığı ilanlardan birinde, proaktif bir yapay zekâ asistanı üzerinde çalışacak kıdemli mühendislik yöneticisi arandığı belirtildi.
Planlanan sistemin kullanıcı adına kod yazabilmesi, internette gezinebilmesi, uygulamaları kontrol edebilmesi ve cihaz üzerinde farklı işlemleri gerçekleştirebilmesi hedefleniyor.
Böylece Apple’ın yapay zekâ sistemini yalnızca soru yanıtlayan veya içerik üreten bir araç olmaktan çıkarıp doğrudan görev yerine getiren bir dijital asistana dönüştürmeyi amaçladığı belirtiliyor.
Apple’ın hamlesi, teknoloji şirketlerinin otonom yapay zekâ ajanlarına yönelik yatırımlarını hızlandırdığı bir dönemde geldi.
Meta’nın Muse adlı aracının restoran rezervasyonu yapma, seyahat planlama ve haber özetleri hazırlama gibi görevleri yerine getirebildiği belirtildi.
Anthropic’in Duet adlı yapay zekâ ajanının kullanıcı testlerini genişlettiği, OpenAI’ın ise Dots’ın yeteneklerini geliştirdiği aktarıldı. Google’ın da Tasks adını verdiği ajanını yenilediği kaydedildi. Apple’ın geliştirdiği sistemin de işletim sistemi arayüzleri içinde otonom biçimde hareket edebilmesi planlanıyor.
Şirketin üzerinde çalıştığı teknolojinin, ChatGPT ve Muse gibi araçların Mac bilgisayarları kontrol etmesini sağlayan sistemlere benzer biçimde çalışacağı belirtildi.
Apple’ın “genel amaçlı bilgisayar kullanım ajanı” olarak tanımladığı sistemin, uygulamalar arasında geçiş yapması, görevleri tamamlaması ve gerektiğinde kullanıcı adına çeşitli dijital işlemleri yürütmesi hedefleniyor.
Bu yaklaşım, klasik sesli asistanlardan farklı olarak yapay zekânın yalnızca komutları anlamasını değil, görevi başından sonuna kadar kendisinin tamamlamasını öngörüyor.
Apple’ın yeni sisteminde gizlilik ve güvenliğin de temel başlıklardan biri olduğu belirtildi.
Şirket, kullanıcı adına kod çalıştırabilen, hesap bilgilerine erişebilen ve işlem gerçekleştirebilen yapay zekâ ajanlarının güçlü izin mekanizmalarıyla sınırlandırılması gerektiğine dikkat çekti.
Bu kapsamda kullanıcı verilerinin korunması, hangi işlemlerin yapay zekâ tarafından gerçekleştirildiğinin açık biçimde gösterilmesi ve kritik işlemlerde ek güvenlik önlemleri uygulanması planlanıyor.
Apple’ın geliştirdiği yapay zekâ ajanının ne zaman kullanıma sunulacağına ilişkin ise henüz bir tarih açıklanmadı.

Waymo and Serve Robotics are walking away from exclusive deals. Can Uber still be the default app for autonomy?
In a late August earnings call, Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi sounded optimistic about his company’s “very strong” partnership with Waymo, the global leader in autonomous robotaxis. The two companies had been working together for years in several cities — including exclusively in Austin and Atlanta — and things were going swimmingly, according to Khosrowshahi.
“We believe we’ll continue to operate next year in those marketplaces,” he gushed. “It’s a terrific product, and the on-the-ground partnership continues to be very strong.”
The partnership would turn out to be more brittle than Khosrowshahi let on. Several weeks later, Waymo co-CEO Tekedra Mawakana revealed in an interview that her company planned to end its exclusive robotaxi partnership with Uber, calling the mixed-fleet experience a “crapshoot” for its own customers. Starting in January 2028, riders in Austin and Atlanta will be able to use the Waymo app to hail driverless rides directly. The unlikely partnership , it would seem, was coming to an end.
Waymo isn’t alone in souring on its experience in the Uber ecosystem. Serve Robotics, which operates thousands of sidewalk delivery robots in dozens of US cities, recently announced it would not renew its partnership with Uber Eats when it expires in 2027.
AI chatbots may be getting all the attention these days, but robotaxis and sidewalk bots are the ones putting in the physical work
AI chatbots may be getting all the attention these days, but robotaxis and sidewalk bots are the ones putting in the physical work. Autonomy is now a true commercial business — albeit an unprofitable one — and the companies building the robots no longer want an intermediary standing between them and their customers. That’s bad news for Uber, which aspires to be the premier robot-powered ridehail and delivery app on the planet.
After Waymo and Serve realized their respective visions for how to operate and bring autonomy to the world differed from Uber’s, the mega platform’s quest looked to be in doubt.
“This thing is real. It used to be a dream,” Serve Robotics CEO Ali Kashani told me recently. “And now you see Waymos everywhere, you see Serve robots everywhere. So some of the tensions about how that future is going to shake out [are] now actually coming to light.”
At first, Uber’s pitch to robotaxi and sidewalk robot operators was simple: Let us help you get off the ground by connecting your vehicles to our massive customer base and encouraging a skeptical public to give them a try. Initially, it seemed like a pretty good deal. If you’re a cash-strapped autonomous vehicle startup, why not piggyback on Uber’s platform, where hundreds of millions of people summon cars or order something delivered every day?
“I call this the Trojan horse,” said Harry Campbell, who writes about the autonomous vehicle industry in his newsletter, The Driverless Digest . “[Uber] introduces the Waymo product to a bunch of actual regular users and riders of Uber who would have never considered AVs.”
It wasn’t just Waymo and Serve that saw the benefit — more than 30 companies around the world have deals with Uber to feature their autonomous vehicles on its app. Amazon’s Zoox just launched with Uber in Las Vegas. China’s WeRide has vehicles operating on the Uber app in Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Riyadh, and Madrid. Avride , the tech startup that spun out of Russia’s Yandex, has both autonomous vehicles and sidewalk robots active on Uber and Uber Eats in Dallas.
This is all part of Uber’s big play to become the default robotaxi and robot delivery app in the world, Khosrowshahi said on that August earnings call. Not just one or two companies — dozens. By 2028, Uber says it expects to have “tens of thousands” of unsupervised AVs, across more than 50 cities. And citing a recent analysis by Jeffries, Uber notes that in cities where robotaxis have been operating for a while (like San Francisco, Phoenix, and Los Angeles), the company’s business is actually growing faster — and capturing a bigger slice of the ride-hailing market — than in the rest of the country.
“[Uber] introduces the Waymo product to a bunch of actual regular users and riders of Uber who would have never considered AVs.”
“We want to make sure that we’re not dependent on one partner,” Khosrowshahi said in August. “We’re absolutely seeing a plethora of newer players in the AV ecosystem, just like you see in the foundation model space.”
The only problem with that strategy is that partners eventually get antsy and want to split off on their own, Campbell said.
“Waymo, I think, kind of held the cards and tried this experiment with Uber,” he said. “And within about six to 12 months, I think they knew it wasn’t working that well.”
One of Waymo’s biggest problems was consistency. Uber’s theory was that customers could hail a ride and get paired with either a robotaxi or a human driver, whichever was closer. But as Waymo discovered, many riders preferred to know exactly what they were getting.
“Early in adoption, predictability matters because many consumers are still forming their first impressions of autonomous vehicles,” TC Eley, an assistant professor of management information systems at the Villanova School of Business, told me in an email. “If riders specifically choose a robotaxi but receive a human driver, they lose an opportunity to learn about the technology on their own terms.”
The flip side can also be true. “If [riders] do not want to ride in a robotaxi but are given one, this first impression may lead to the customer having a negative experience and not wanting to ride in an AV in the future,” Eley added.
Uber has since pushed back on the idea that it wasn’t willing to adapt to Waymo’s needs. According to Bloomberg, the ridehail company pitched the idea of a dedicated robotaxi button in its app for Austin and Atlanta — but Waymo declined the offer. (A Waymo spokesperson didn’t reply to a request for comment.)
Serve, which operates more than 2,000 sidewalk robots as the second-largest autonomous fleet in the US behind Waymo, illustrates a similar dynamic. Rather than renew its partnership with Uber Eats, the company launched a direct developer API allowing any small business to build its own robot delivery service using Serve’s fleet.
The decision, according to Kashani, was largely economic. Delivery apps like DoorDash and Uber Eats take a massive 15 percent to 30 percent cut on every order, largely because paying human couriers is expensive. By letting businesses connect directly to its fleet through software, Serve wants to let local shops — like bakeries, florists, and pharmacies — add robot delivery straight to their own websites and checkout registers without paying steep middleman fees.
“At least in our case, there was a different vision for how we wanted to operate and kind of bring this to the world versus how Uber wanted to,” Kashani said. “They’re doing what’s right for their business, and we’re going to do what’s right for ours.”
In a statement, Uber spokesperson Noah Edwardsen said the fault lies with Serve, not Uber.
“We believe autonomy will be a key part of the future of both delivery and mobility, and we continue to scale with many partners around the world,” Edwardsen said. “Beginning in early 2026, we repeatedly raised concerns to Serve about operational performance and reliability, and unfortunately performance did not improve to the level we required.”
It wasn’t long ago that Waymo and Uber were locked in a bitter standoff over the future of autonomous vehicles.
In 2017, the Alphabet-owned company sued Uber over allegations of trade secret theft and patent infringement. The case went to trial a year later but ended abruptly when the two sides reached a surprise settlement after just a week of testimony. Uber later admitted that it misappropriated some of Waymo’s tech and agreed to license it for future use.…
